_about: Route search vectors (trains design 4): a small network of made-up track parts (`parts`, connections as in track-network.json; bricks give where each connection is, `points`, at orientation 0 unless `orientation` says) — a passing loop between two points, a reversing loop, a separate piece and a stub line (`bricks`, which train-geometry.json uses too); and a second network (`loopBricks`, the cases with `network: "loops"`): an oval, an oval with a hairline gap (joined for trains), a figure eight, a dog bone (a reversing loop at each end), two straights too far apart to join, and part of a real layout, Fordyce 2026 (its real parts) round to a siding across a hairline gap — and searches (`facing`: which way the train leaves the start, either when left out) with what both apps must find: the steps (brick, from, to), the length (studs), the switch settings the route needs, the bricks it runs both ways (turnsAround), which way it leaves the start (facing) and the switches it needs set both ways (bothWays), or the problem (noTrack, turnAround). `gaps`: the loose ends of the loops network that nearly meet (joined for trains). `status` is the saved route checked again on the network with brick M taken out (broken at a step, or still ok; the loops: on the same network). Web packages/parts-catalog/src/track/routes.test.ts (BLD_WRITE_CONTRACTS=1 writes `expect` and `status`), desktop tests/track/RoutesTest.cpp.
